newsitem.title: USA: Stocks end lower on profit-taking after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Stocks end lower on profit-taking after recent gains.

text.p: Stocks lost ground Wednesday as investors called time out after the market's recent string of records and also on disappointment that Intel Corp. shares fell despite the company's strong earnings.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended 35.41 points lower at 6,726.88, snapping a four session streak of record closes.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,257 to 1,256 on active volume of 524 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 12.83 at 1,333.53, or nearly 1 percent, as technology stocks were especially hard hit, reversing their powerful gains on Tuesday.
"Today was a mirror image of yesterday," said Tom Carpenter, managing director at ASB Capital Management Inc. "Let's face it, there have been phenomenal returns in stocks."
International Business Machines Corp. slipped 2-3/4 to 164-1/4, the steepest loss among Dow components.

Perhaps more disappointing for investors, however, was a stiff sell-off in Intel, which skidded 5-1/8 to 142, one day after the world's largest semiconductor maker reported fourth quarter earnings that far exceeded Wall Street estimates.

While some of the selling in Intel reflected the same profit-taking impulse that afflicted the entire tech sector, some of the pressure came from concern that Intel's results had finally set a standard that even the company itself could no longer surpass.
Several analysts adjusted their future earnings estimates on Intel.

In an unexpected step, Cowen & Co. took the additional step of downgrading Intel's stock, citing concern about the company's capacity to sustain gross profit margins and revenue growth in the first quarter of this year.
Interest rates were another source of pressure for stocks, as the bond market relinquished some of its recent gains in the absence of any significant economic news.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lost 9/32, raising its yield to 6.79 percent from 6.77 percent at Tuesday's close.

Among pockets of strength was the transportation sector. The Dow Jones transportion index jumped 29.90 points, or 1.32 percent, to 2,299.13, boosted by Delta Air Lines's comments about strong growth in revenues.
Delta Air leaped 3-1/4 to 75-1/4 after it also said its costs in the latest quarter would be less than earlier expected.
United Airlines parent UAL Corp. rose 1-5/8 to 58, Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp. gained 2-3/4 to 89-1/2 and Conrail Inc. advanced 1-1/8 to 103-1/2.
Medical device maker St. Jude Medical Inc. dropped 1-7/8 to 37 on concerns that the company and other firms in the same business may not meet fourth-quarter earnings expectations.
Tencor Instruments shot up 5-3/8 to 35-7/8 on news of its agreement to merge with semiconductor equipment maker KLA Instruments Corp., which shed 3/8 to 40-1/2.

Internet navigational service Yahoo Inc. rose 4-1/2 to 25-3/8 after Hambrecht & Quist upgraded its rating on the stock. Late Tuesday Yahoo reported a profit of $96,000 for the fourth quarter vs. a loss of $1.15 million in the third quarter.
Clarify Inc. shares tumbled 11-1/2 to 34-1/2 after the software company's quarterly earnings disappointed some investors.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 1.66 points to 767.20. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 1.87 to 586.48.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.03 to 405.04. The average share was unchanged.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,426.467 down 11.652 or 0.16 percent.
